title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 4th version, 1986). X is a set and (X_i)_{i in I} is a family of subsets indexed by a poset I. Grothendieck defines the boundary ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j and the 'open cell' X_i° = X_i \ ∂X_i. A 'figure ensembliste' indexed by I is a combinatorial, set-level model of a cell or stratified decomposition. Its axioms are:
- 2') the open cells are pairwise disjoint and (as the following page makes explicit, via b')) non-empty;
- the open cells cover X;
- 3') X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
The proposition under proof says these are equivalent to (ii) X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k, together with the covering condition.

This page finishes (ii)⇒3'). On the previous page he took x in X_i, chose j with x in X_j°, and reduced to showing X_j° ⊂ X_i. Here he proves X_j° ∩ X_i ≠ ∅ ⇒ j ≤ i:
- X_j° ∩ X_i ⊂ X_j ∩ X_i = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k.
- If j ≰ i, then every k ≤ i,j satisfies k ≠ j, hence k < j. So X_k ⊂ ∂X_j ⊂ ∁X_j°.
- Thus X_j° ∩ X_i is contained in its own complement, so it is empty. This contradicts the hypothesis that it is non-empty.
Once j ≤ i, (ii) with k = j gives X_j ⊂ X_i, hence X_j° ⊂ X_i. 'La prop. est prouvée.'

Corollary 3 is heavily reworked with many crossed-out attempts. It gives a local characterization: (X_i) is a figure ensembliste indexed by I iff
- b) the open cells are non-empty and pairwise disjoint (the margin NB splits this into b') X_i° ≠ ∅ and b'') i ≠ j ⇒ X_i° ∩ X_j° = ∅);
- c) for each i, the subfamily 𝔛_i = {X_j : j ≤ i} of 𝔓(X) is a figure ensembliste (in X_i).
Crossed-out attempts include:
- a weaker 'quasi-admissible' condition;
- X_i ⊂ X_j ⇔ i ≤ j;
- X_i° = X_i \ ∪_{j≤i, X_j≠X_i} X_j, i.e. the open cell computed intrinsically in 𝔛_i.
The next page carries out the proof: it identifies the intrinsic cells of 𝔛_i with the X_j° and shows X_i ⊂ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j.

In modern terms, a figure ensembliste is the same as a surjection s: X → I, with X_i° = s^{-1}(i) and X_i = s^{-1}(↓i). Equivalently it is a poset-stratified set, i.e. the pullback of the Alexandrov topology. The work serves to build a purely combinatorial foundation for cell or stratified decompositions in the 'Analysis situs' chapter.
errors: The conclusion should read 'contradicts the hypothesis that it is non-empty' (X_j°∩X_i ≠ ∅); the transcription's 'vide' is either an abbreviation or a slip.
The covering hypothesis ∪X_i° = X is needed for 3') but is added only as an afterthought; the previous page notes it in the lemma.

Corollary 3 is left in a messy, partly crossed-out state. The precise final formulation of condition c), especially in which ambient set the subfamily 𝔛_i is a figure, is not cleanly stated on this page. No real mathematical error, though.

ideas.what: Set-theoretic 'figure': a poset-indexed family of subsets with boundary ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i}X_j and open cells X_i° = X_i\∂X_i, the cells partitioning X and closures being downward unions of cells
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified set / decomposition indexed by a face poset (surjection X→I, Alexandrov topology pullback)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; face posets of regular CW complexes (Björner 1984); poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Higher Algebra, appendix A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures only programmatically; this formalism is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Equivalence of the intersection formula X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j}X_k (plus covering) with disjointness of cells and X_i = ∪_{j≤i}X_j°, via 'X_j°∩X_i≠∅ ⇒ j≤i'
ideas.modern_name: closure-finite / frontier condition for stratifications, combinatorial version
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Whitney/Thom frontier condition in a topological setting)

ideas.what: Local characterization (Corollary 3): global figure iff cells are non-empty and disjoint and each down-truncated subfamily is a figure
ideas.modern_name: locality of cellular structure (checking on closed cells)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains careful but elementary combinatorial bookkeeping for a set-level notion of cellular or stratified decomposition. The notion is equivalent to a surjection onto a poset, which is standard (Alexandrov topology, face posets). It is interesting only as documentation of how Grothendieck laid the foundations of his 1986 'Analysis situs'; no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 'ce qui contredit l'hyp. que c'est vide' should be read as contradicting non-emptiness (X_j°∩X_i ≠ ∅).
The condition 'X_j^0 ∩ X_i ≠ ∅ ⟹ j ≤ i' is correctly transcribed; X^0 is Grothendieck's X° (open cell).
Margin NB (left, vertical): 'b) équivaut à b') ∀i∈I, X_i°≠∅ et b'') ∀i,j, i≠j, X_i°∩X_j°=∅'. Second margin NB: 'La condition b) signifie que X = ∪X_i°' (approx.).
In Corollary 3 the line '𝔛_i ⊂ 𝔓(X)' belongs to the definition of 𝔛_i in condition c) (the set of the X_j, j ≤ i), not to b).
Crossed-out formula at bottom: 'X_i° = intérieur [cellule ouverte] de X_i dans 𝔛_i = X_i \ ∪_{j≤i, X_j≠X_i} X_j'.
